pr_title: fix: safe loading of content type name `then`
pr_body:
### What does it do?

Allows the use of the content type name "then" by not including model names as root property names returned by promises.

**I do not know if we want to merge this**, because it could potentially lead to very difficult to debug issues in the future if we ever have another case where the content type name is a key for a function. Although currently everything works fine. I was curious about this bug and got lost down a rabbit-hole and wanted a demo of it 😆

Calling this an enhancement, because it literally only happens with the `then` keyword and we've blocked that already in the CTB. Although it's kind of a fix, because we only restrict `then` in the CTB and someone adding it to their schema directly is still unable to start up Strapi.

### Why is it needed?

Node Promises consider any object with a `then` property that is a function to be a promise, and tries to execute it when awaited. When we were loading dynamic content type names asynchronously and the result included a key called 'then' from a content type named such, it would try to execute it as code, causing a crash because createCoreController was called during this file loading instead of later as intended.

### How to test it?

Create a content type named "then" and everything should work.

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

Fixes https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/15557

DX-1396

issue_context.title: Having a content-type with the name `then` causes Strapi to be unable to start
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
Having a content-type with the name `then` causes Strapi to be unable to start

### Required System information

<!-- Please ensure you are using the Node LTS version (v14 or v16 or v18) -->
<!-- Strapi v3 is not supported unless it is a critical/high security issue -->

- Node.js version: v18.13.0
- NPM version: 8.19.3
- Strapi version: 4.5.6
- Database: sqlite
- Operating system: OSX

### Describe the bug

A clear and concise description of what the bug is.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Using the Content-Type Builder
1. create a new content type with the Display name `Then`
2. Add a text field called `Title`
3. Save the content-type

Strapi will be unable to restart and emits the following error:
```
[2023-01-24 12:07:35.671] debug: ⛔️ Server wasn't able to start properly.
[2023-01-24 12:07:35.673] error: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'contentType')
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'contentType')
    at Object.then (.../node_modules/@strapi/strapi/lib/factories.js:12:27)
```

### Expected behavior

I expected Strapi to restart and use my new content type

### Additional context

Having chatted with the folks on open office hours in Discord, the idea seems to be that `then` is a reserved word either in sqlite  or Strapi itself. We chatted about not allowing a user to enter a reserved word as an api name through the editor.
comments: I can confirm and replicate the issue with replications staps

review_comments: by making the function async aren't you removing the need for that result 🤔  if you await loadFile now it won't be calling then on any of the imported code because it's wrapped I think
Yeah, I got the whole problem wrong because it seemed that something weird within importDefault was making it async sometimes, but that wasn't actually the case.

Ok, nevermind, I checked.  I did have a useless await on `importDefault` but `readJSON` is async, that's why I put it explicitly.

So everything else needs to be here. Including this `result`, because `await Promise.all` waits for all the nested promises to settle, meaning it tries to call the `.then()` from loadFIles, even if it were made sync with `readJSONSync`. So we have to add this layer where there is no function called 'then' or it will get called
Arf ok I thought we could avoid it 🤷

So the big question is, is allowing this worth a risk that someone could make a similar bug in the future? I could add an api test with a content type called "then" but it almost feel a bit silly to work on this considering it's just one keyword we can ban. I actually did this "as a community member" on the weekend for that reason 😆

good question, the way I see it, with dynamic import it's a good fix to wrap into results in case someone accidentaly puts a then() or any other function we might missinterpret. 

However banning node keywords as a whole would be a good safety measure as we do generate a lot of code. If we didn't have all that customizability sure we could allow more things but here we don't really have a choice as a general principle
Ok, I'll leave `then` restricted (for now) and merge the actual fix, with a note that it's only restricted because it's a keyword but no longer an issue
